originalFailure.summary: tests 2016, pass 1990, fail 1, skipped 25; a green run reports tests 2022
originalFailure.whatTheLogShows: Only the first 3 of the file's 10 subtests were reported (7271 ms, 3572 ms, 2551 ms, each about 2x the solo time), then '✖ table-windows.test.ts (21258 ms)' with only 'test failed'. Subtests 4-10 never reported. The int2 note that 'every subtest passed' is inexact: the file's test process stopped during subtest 4 ('TP1: another file kept in the workspace while the job reads does not stop it') and printed nothing on stderr.
originalFailure.windowsEventLog: No Application Error (1000) or WER crash event for node.exe between 16:30 and 17:40 on 22 October; WER does record native crashes on this machine (git.exe 11:41, other programs), so a native crash of the node process is unlikely.

deathModesCompared.method: Three throwaway node:test files in the scratchpad, run with the spec reporter on node v24.19.0
deathModesCompared.terminatedFromOutside: silent '✖ <file>' with only 'test failed' (taskkill /F on the test process)
deathModesCompared.v8HeapOutOfMemory: prints 'FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit ...' and a native stack; does not match
deathModesCompared.conclusion: The original signature matches an abrupt exit or an outside termination of the file's process during subtest 4. It does not match a leftover timer or handle (that keeps a process alive and does not fail it), an unhandled rejection or 'asynchronous activity after the test ended' (these print text, and later subtests still report), or a heap OOM (prints text).

suspectsChecked.finding: readOriginal (table-profile-worker.ts) clears its 30 s lease-renewal setInterval in finally; openObjectStream (infrastructure/storage.ts) unrefs and clears its timeout; the test uses transaction() without a deadline, so db.ts deadline timers are not armed; the workbook reader child (tabular-stream.ts readWorkbookWindows) is killed if still running and its close is awaited in finally. An open handle would keep the process alive, not fail it.

suspectsChecked.suspect: unhandled promise rejection after a test ends
suspectsChecked.finding: Every call in the file is awaited; the in-flight heartbeat rejection is caught (.catch destroys the body). An after-end rejection would print a 'generated asynchronous activity after the test ended' warning and later subtests would still report.

suspectsChecked.suspect: shared module state, temp path or port
suspectsChecked.finding: Each test runs in its own process (node:test process isolation). Scratch folders are mkdtemp under the root (tmpdir() for CSV; ULPIN_DOCUMENT_OCR_SCRATCH=tmp/ulpin-table-scratch-windows for XW1, which no other file uses); only that mkdtemp folder is removed. S3 is mocked (endpoint 127.0.0.1:1 is never opened); the pool is a stub in globalThis. No port is listened on.
No process.exitCode or process.exit in packages/server/src.
node:test has no default per-test or per-file timeout (Infinity); a timeout would be reported on the subtest with text. Subtests ran up to 2x slower under load and still passed.

fix: none: no concrete defect found in the test or the code it tests, and the failure did not recur in 11 concurrent runs
nextIfItRecurs: Run the backend set with --test-reporter=tap (the TAP YAML of a file-level failure carries exitCode and signal). Exit code 1 with no text points to TerminateProcess from outside the test process; then check what else ran on the machine at that minute.
